userSources.text: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.

Keep this minimal: the default player avatar, selected stationary dummy, one punch action with its animation, successful-hit sound, and hit counter. Use a plain floor and the default Roblox camera. Remove the reset-counter control, dummy flinch, arena decoration, movement restrictions, and custom clothing. The selected assets provide the appearance. Keep the counter for this play session. Preserve the selected assets and keep all three proposal sections consistent with these limits.

Core loop: the player (default Roblox avatar) faces the selected stationary target dummy asset. Pressing a single 'Punch' input (default: left mouse click or gamepad face button A / keyboard Space) triggers a punch action if the player is not already mid-punch (no combo chaining). The punch action plays a forward jab animation lasting roughly 0.3-0.5 seconds (windup, strike, recovery). A hit is registered when the punch's active strike frame overlaps the dummy's hitbox. On a successful hit: (1) a punch/hit sound effect plays once, (2) the on-screen hit counter increments by exactly 1. A brief cooldown ensures only one hit is registered per punch swing, even if overlap persists across multiple frames. The dummy has no health, cannot be defeated, never attacks back, and shows no flinch or reactive animation. There is no reset-counter control; the counter persists for the play session and resets only on scene reload/restart. Player movement uses standard default Roblox movement controls (WASD/left stick) with no added arena boundaries or movement restrictions beyond the default playable space; no jumping or blocking mechanics are included in this scope.
Single-player only; no multiplayer, AI opponent behavior, or networking.
Dummy is purely stationary and cannot be damaged, destroyed, or knocked over, and has no flinch or reactive animation.
Only one punch type/animation is required (no combos, kicks, blocks, or special moves) per the request scope.
Hit counter is a simple integer displayed as on-screen UI text (e.g., 'Hits: 0') anchored to a screen corner.
Counter increments exactly once per successful punch connection using a per-swing hit-registered flag.
Default control scheme: standard Roblox movement plus one button for punching; no reset-counter input or button is included.
No scoring, timer, win condition, or difficulty progression is required; this is a practice/demo loop.
Punch and hit use the same single sound effect (no separate whiff vs. connect sounds) unless later expanded.
Player avatar and dummy appearance are provided entirely by the selected default/selected Roblox assets; no custom clothing or rig modifications are required.
Camera uses the default Roblox third-person follow camera; no fixed framing or custom camera control is implemented.

A lighthearted training-gym aesthetic: the player is a boxer/martial artist in practice gear (tank top, wraps or gloves, shorts) working out in a no-frills gym corner. The target dummy is a classic red-and-black canvas heavy-bag-style humanoid dummy mounted on a weighted base, evoking boxing gyms and arcade punch-meter machines. Tone is upbeat and casual, not violent or gory — this is presented as a training/fitness minigame rather than a combat-to-defeat scenario, reinforced by the dummy's harmless flinch reaction and the absence of health bars or damage numbers. Sound design leans into satisfying 'thwack'/glove-impact punch sounds reminiscent of classic arcade boxing games. The on-screen hit counter is styled like a gym rep-counter or arcade score display (bold numerals, simple font) to reinforce the training-drill framing.
Visual tone is stylized/cartoonish rather than photorealistic or gory, keeping the experience family-friendly.
Player and dummy character models are generic/unbranded (no licensed characters or IP references).
Setting is a single indoor gym-style room; no outdoor or narrative story elements are needed.
No dialogue, voiceover, or narrative text is required beyond the hit counter UI.
Color palette and lighting are simple/bright (gym lighting) rather than dramatic or moody, matching the low-stakes training theme.

Layout is a plain flat floor with no additional decoration, props, or themed backdrop. The selected stationary target dummy asset is placed at a fixed point on the floor; the player spawns using the default Roblox avatar a short distance away, within comfortable punching range after a short walk. The on-screen hit counter UI is anchored to a fixed screen-space position (e.g., top-center or top-right) so it remains visible during gameplay. The scene uses the default Roblox camera (third-person follow) with no custom framing. There are no invisible walls, arena boundaries, or added movement restrictions; the player can move freely across the plain floor using standard default movement, relying on default Roblox physics and collision.
Single static scene; no level transitions, multiple rooms, or loading between areas.
Play space is a plain floor with no decorative props, backdrop, or themed environment art; only the selected dummy asset and default avatar are present.
Lighting uses Roblox default lighting; no custom or dynamic lighting rigs are configured.
No destructible or interactive environment props beyond the dummy itself in this scope.
No arena boundaries or invisible walls are added; player movement is unrestricted beyond the standard default playable area.

playerExperience.title: Punch the Dummy: Training Drill
playerExperience.summary: A minimal single-player boxing-gym practice loop. The player spawns on a plain, undecorated floor a short walk from a stationary training dummy (selected asset 1245720733), using the default Roblox avatar, default third-person camera and default WASD/gamepad movement with no arena boundaries. Pressing the single punch input (left click, Space, or gamepad A) triggers a forward jab (R15 Punching Animations asset 12061946559, clip 1/1/18/1) lasting roughly 0.3-0.5s (windup/strike/recovery) if the player is not already mid-punch. The server authoritatively checks the strike-frame overlap against the dummy's hitbox; on a confirmed hit it plays the Punch Impact 1 sound (asset 132504023010884) once and increments a persistent on-screen 'Hits: N' counter by exactly 1, gated by a per-swing hit-registered flag so only one hit registers per swing even under sustained overlap. The dummy has no health, never flinches, never attacks, and cannot be defeated or moved. There is no reset-counter control; the count persists for the session and only clears on scene reload. No combos, kicks, blocks, scoring, timers or win conditions are included. First minute: player spawns near the dummy on the plain floor, sees the 'Hits: 0' counter top-of-screen, walks up, punches, hears/see the jab animation and impact sound, and watches the counter climb with each successful connect - a simple, satisfying training-drill loop.
playerExperience.visualDirection: Bright, simple default Roblox lighting evokes a no-frills gym corner - no custom lighting rigs, fog, or moody color grading. The only authored visual elements are the imported dummy's own red-and-black canvas heavy-bag styling (asset-provided, not recolored) and a plain flat gray/neutral floor with zero decorative props or backdrop. The HUD is a single bold 'Hits: N' text label anchored to a fixed screen corner (top-center or top-right), styled like a simple arcade rep-counter (bold sans numerals, high-contrast color against a small translucent backing frame) but otherwise unadorned - no meters, health bars, or damage numbers. Player and dummy appearance come entirely from the default Roblox avatar and the selected dummy asset; no custom clothing, rig edits, or added accessories. Camera is the untouched default third-person follow camera.

A lighthearted training-gym aesthetic: the player is a boxer/martial artist in practice gear (tank top, wraps or gloves, shorts) working out in a no-frills gym corner. The target dummy is a classic red-and-black canvas heavy-bag-style humanoid dummy mounted on a weighted base, evoking boxing gyms and arcade punch-meter machines. Tone is upbeat and casual, not violent or gory — this is presented as a training/fitness minigame rather than a combat-to-defeat scenario, reinforced by the dummy's harmless flinch reaction and the absence of health bars or damage numbers. Sound design leans into satisfying 'thwack'/glove-impact punch sounds reminiscent of classic arcade boxing games. The on-screen hit counter is styled like a gym rep-counter or arcade score display (bold numerals, simple font) to reinforce the training-drill framing.
Visual tone is stylized/cartoonish rather than photorealistic or gory, keeping the experience family-friendly.
Player and dummy character models are generic/unbranded (no licensed characters or IP references).
Setting is a single indoor gym-style room; no outdoor or narrative story elements are needed.
No dialogue, voiceover, or narrative text is required beyond the hit counter UI.
Color palette and lighting are simple/bright (gym lighting) rather than dramatic or moody, matching the low-stakes training theme.

runtimeReference.textures: Texture and Decal are supported. Face requires {type:"Enum",enum:"NormalId",value:1} for Top, never enum:"Top". Discover requested images through the Marketplace asset pipeline, preferably as part of a complete reusable component. Inspect and verify the selected image before integration. Do not invent IDs or require the user to supply an image that the worker can discover. If retrieval or verification cannot complete, report the specific gap instead of claiming a replacement satisfies the request.

hierarchy.rule: Manifest slash paths describe separate nested Instances. FindFirstChild and WaitForChild take ONE child name, never a slash path. Never create a Folder whose name combines namespace and /children. Script filenames lose .server.luau, .client.luau, .module.luau or .luau at runtime. Example: BuffUtils.module.luau becomes BuffUtils.

runtimeReference.sceneProperties: Name and Parent come from the path: omit both from properties. BasePart uses Color (Color3 value), Size (Vector3), CFrame, Anchored and CanCollide; it has no Color3 or Scale property. Set a walkable ground surface and a collidable spawn. LocalScripts run in StarterGui or StarterPlayerScripts; shared ModuleScripts in ReplicatedStorage are required explicitly.

references.rule: Part0, Part1, PrimaryPart, Attachment0/1 and Adornee use {type:'Ref',path:'exact scene path'}, never strings or nested Instances. Null path clears a reference. All referenced nodes must be declared in this bundle or existing dependencies. References resolve after construction, so forward references work. Humanoid, Animator, AnimationController, Motor6D, Weld, WeldConstraint and Highlight are supported scene classes. Motor6D requires BasePart Part0/Part1 and CFrame C0/C1. Models containing a Humanoid need a connected, unanchored rig to move, not just disconnected decorative parts.

runtimeReference.animation: Resize individual Parts with Size, recolor with Color, and animate via TweenService:Create(part, TweenInfo.new(seconds), {Size=targetSize, Color=targetColor}). Models scale with ScaleTo(number) and move with PivotTo(CFrame). Do not invent Part.Scale. Keep a crop's bottom above its soil while changing height.
runtimeReference.interactions: ProximityPrompt.Triggered connects on the server and supplies player. Validate humanoid health, distance, rate limits, ownership and current state on the server. Do not trust client attributes or RemoteEvent payloads. Per-player state requires indexing by player/UserId, not just a shared object name; clean associated objects and connections when they leave.
runtimeReference.presentation: A ScreenGui belongs in PlayerGui at runtime; LocalScripts may create it there. Put GUI Frames inside a ScreenGui, not directly inside PlayerGui. For a ResetOnSpawn=false HUD, keep its controller in StarterPlayerScripts or inside that persistent ScreenGui. A LocalScript directly under a StarterGui Folder restarts after respawn and can create duplicate, stale HUDs. Rebind health subscriptions on CharacterAdded and disconnect old connections. Send initial state after the client is ready, or use replicated attributes/value objects that the HUD reads initially and observes for changes. A one-time FireClient during PlayerAdded can be missed.
runtimeReference.audio: Audio is Marketplace-only. Discover complete reusable components first, preserving included sound references and provenance; search separately for missing sounds. Audio must pass the asset pipeline's loading, playback and listening checks before acceptance. Built-in, generated, placeholder and procedural audio are not permitted fallbacks. If verified audio is unavailable, report the unmet requirement rather than silently substituting sound. Do not invent IDs or claim unperformed playback tests.
runtimeReference.verification: FindFirstChild absence is a failure when an object is required: assert its presence before checking behavior. Tests must not skip absent objects, compare fabricated state tables, or call nonexistent signal Fire methods. Keep tests out of the live player loop; use the protected review harness for acceptance tests. Report untestable interactions honestly.

spec.title: Punch the Dummy: Training Drill
spec.summary: A minimal single-player boxing-gym practice loop. The player spawns on a plain, undecorated floor a short walk from a stationary training dummy (selected asset 1245720733), using the default Roblox avatar, default third-person camera and default WASD/gamepad movement with no arena boundaries. Pressing the single punch input (left click, Space, or gamepad A) triggers a forward jab (R15 Punching Animations asset 12061946559, clip 1/1/18/1) lasting roughly 0.3-0.5s (windup/strike/recovery) if the player is not already mid-punch. The server authoritatively checks the strike-frame overlap against the dummy's hitbox; on a confirmed hit it plays the Punch Impact 1 sound (asset 132504023010884) once and increments a persistent on-screen 'Hits: N' counter by exactly 1, gated by a per-swing hit-registered flag so only one hit registers per swing even under sustained overlap. The dummy has no health, never flinches, never attacks, and cannot be defeated or moved. There is no reset-counter control; the count persists for the session and only clears on scene reload. No combos, kicks, blocks, scoring, timers or win conditions are included. First minute: player spawns near the dummy on the plain floor, sees the 'Hits: 0' counter top-of-screen, walks up, punches, hears/see the jab animation and impact sound, and watches the counter climb with each successful connect - a simple, satisfying training-drill loop.
spec.visualDirection: Bright, simple default Roblox lighting evokes a no-frills gym corner - no custom lighting rigs, fog, or moody color grading. The only authored visual elements are the imported dummy's own red-and-black canvas heavy-bag styling (asset-provided, not recolored) and a plain flat gray/neutral floor with zero decorative props or backdrop. The HUD is a single bold 'Hits: N' text label anchored to a fixed screen corner (top-center or top-right), styled like a simple arcade rep-counter (bold sans numerals, high-contrast color against a small translucent backing frame) but otherwise unadorned - no meters, health bars, or damage numbers. Player and dummy appearance come entirely from the default Roblox avatar and the selected dummy asset; no custom clothing, rig edits, or added accessories. Camera is the untouched default third-person follow camera.

A lighthearted training-gym aesthetic: the player is a boxer/martial artist in practice gear (tank top, wraps or gloves, shorts) working out in a no-frills gym corner. The target dummy is a classic red-and-black canvas heavy-bag-style humanoid dummy mounted on a weighted base, evoking boxing gyms and arcade punch-meter machines. Tone is upbeat and casual, not violent or gory — this is presented as a training/fitness minigame rather than a combat-to-defeat scenario, reinforced by the dummy's harmless flinch reaction and the absence of health bars or damage numbers. Sound design leans into satisfying 'thwack'/glove-impact punch sounds reminiscent of classic arcade boxing games. The on-screen hit counter is styled like a gym rep-counter or arcade score display (bold numerals, simple font) to reinforce the training-drill framing.
Visual tone is stylized/cartoonish rather than photorealistic or gory, keeping the experience family-friendly.
Player and dummy character models are generic/unbranded (no licensed characters or IP references).
Setting is a single indoor gym-style room; no outdoor or narrative story elements are needed.
No dialogue, voiceover, or narrative text is required beyond the hit counter UI.
Color palette and lighting are simple/bright (gym lighting) rather than dramatic or moody, matching the low-stakes training theme.

userSources.text: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.

Keep this minimal: the default player avatar, selected stationary dummy, one punch action with its animation, successful-hit sound, and hit counter. Use a plain floor and the default Roblox camera. Remove the reset-counter control, dummy flinch, arena decoration, movement restrictions, and custom clothing. The selected assets provide the appearance. Keep the counter for this play session. Preserve the selected assets and keep all three proposal sections consistent with these limits.

Core loop: the player (default Roblox avatar) faces the selected stationary target dummy asset. Pressing a single 'Punch' input (default: left mouse click or gamepad face button A / keyboard Space) triggers a punch action if the player is not already mid-punch (no combo chaining). The punch action plays a forward jab animation lasting roughly 0.3-0.5 seconds (windup, strike, recovery). A hit is registered when the punch's active strike frame overlaps the dummy's hitbox. On a successful hit: (1) a punch/hit sound effect plays once, (2) the on-screen hit counter increments by exactly 1. A brief cooldown ensures only one hit is registered per punch swing, even if overlap persists across multiple frames. The dummy has no health, cannot be defeated, never attacks back, and shows no flinch or reactive animation. There is no reset-counter control; the counter persists for the play session and resets only on scene reload/restart. Player movement uses standard default Roblox movement controls (WASD/left stick) with no added arena boundaries or movement restrictions beyond the default playable space; no jumping or blocking mechanics are included in this scope.
Single-player only; no multiplayer, AI opponent behavior, or networking.
Dummy is purely stationary and cannot be damaged, destroyed, or knocked over, and has no flinch or reactive animation.
Only one punch type/animation is required (no combos, kicks, blocks, or special moves) per the request scope.
Hit counter is a simple integer displayed as on-screen UI text (e.g., 'Hits: 0') anchored to a screen corner.
Counter increments exactly once per successful punch connection using a per-swing hit-registered flag.
Default control scheme: standard Roblox movement plus one button for punching; no reset-counter input or button is included.
No scoring, timer, win condition, or difficulty progression is required; this is a practice/demo loop.
Punch and hit use the same single sound effect (no separate whiff vs. connect sounds) unless later expanded.
Player avatar and dummy appearance are provided entirely by the selected default/selected Roblox assets; no custom clothing or rig modifications are required.
Camera uses the default Roblox third-person follow camera; no fixed framing or custom camera control is implemented.

A lighthearted training-gym aesthetic: the player is a boxer/martial artist in practice gear (tank top, wraps or gloves, shorts) working out in a no-frills gym corner. The target dummy is a classic red-and-black canvas heavy-bag-style humanoid dummy mounted on a weighted base, evoking boxing gyms and arcade punch-meter machines. Tone is upbeat and casual, not violent or gory — this is presented as a training/fitness minigame rather than a combat-to-defeat scenario, reinforced by the dummy's harmless flinch reaction and the absence of health bars or damage numbers. Sound design leans into satisfying 'thwack'/glove-impact punch sounds reminiscent of classic arcade boxing games. The on-screen hit counter is styled like a gym rep-counter or arcade score display (bold numerals, simple font) to reinforce the training-drill framing.
Visual tone is stylized/cartoonish rather than photorealistic or gory, keeping the experience family-friendly.
Player and dummy character models are generic/unbranded (no licensed characters or IP references).
Setting is a single indoor gym-style room; no outdoor or narrative story elements are needed.
No dialogue, voiceover, or narrative text is required beyond the hit counter UI.
Color palette and lighting are simple/bright (gym lighting) rather than dramatic or moody, matching the low-stakes training theme.

Layout is a plain flat floor with no additional decoration, props, or themed backdrop. The selected stationary target dummy asset is placed at a fixed point on the floor; the player spawns using the default Roblox avatar a short distance away, within comfortable punching range after a short walk. The on-screen hit counter UI is anchored to a fixed screen-space position (e.g., top-center or top-right) so it remains visible during gameplay. The scene uses the default Roblox camera (third-person follow) with no custom framing. There are no invisible walls, arena boundaries, or added movement restrictions; the player can move freely across the plain floor using standard default movement, relying on default Roblox physics and collision.
Single static scene; no level transitions, multiple rooms, or loading between areas.
Play space is a plain floor with no decorative props, backdrop, or themed environment art; only the selected dummy asset and default avatar are present.
Lighting uses Roblox default lighting; no custom or dynamic lighting rigs are configured.
No destructible or interactive environment props beyond the dummy itself in this scope.
No arena boundaries or invisible walls are added; player movement is unrestricted beyond the standard default playable area.

playerExperience.title: Punch the Dummy: Training Drill
playerExperience.summary: A minimal single-player boxing-gym practice loop. The player spawns on a plain, undecorated floor a short walk from a stationary training dummy (selected asset 1245720733), using the default Roblox avatar, default third-person camera and default WASD/gamepad movement with no arena boundaries. Pressing the single punch input (left click, Space, or gamepad A) triggers a forward jab (R15 Punching Animations asset 12061946559, clip 1/1/18/1) lasting roughly 0.3-0.5s (windup/strike/recovery) if the player is not already mid-punch. The server authoritatively checks the strike-frame overlap against the dummy's hitbox; on a confirmed hit it plays the Punch Impact 1 sound (asset 132504023010884) once and increments a persistent on-screen 'Hits: N' counter by exactly 1, gated by a per-swing hit-registered flag so only one hit registers per swing even under sustained overlap. The dummy has no health, never flinches, never attacks, and cannot be defeated or moved. There is no reset-counter control; the count persists for the session and only clears on scene reload. No combos, kicks, blocks, scoring, timers or win conditions are included. First minute: player spawns near the dummy on the plain floor, sees the 'Hits: 0' counter top-of-screen, walks up, punches, hears/see the jab animation and impact sound, and watches the counter climb with each successful connect - a simple, satisfying training-drill loop.
playerExperience.visualDirection: Bright, simple default Roblox lighting evokes a no-frills gym corner - no custom lighting rigs, fog, or moody color grading. The only authored visual elements are the imported dummy's own red-and-black canvas heavy-bag styling (asset-provided, not recolored) and a plain flat gray/neutral floor with zero decorative props or backdrop. The HUD is a single bold 'Hits: N' text label anchored to a fixed screen corner (top-center or top-right), styled like a simple arcade rep-counter (bold sans numerals, high-contrast color against a small translucent backing frame) but otherwise unadorned - no meters, health bars, or damage numbers. Player and dummy appearance come entirely from the default Roblox avatar and the selected dummy asset; no custom clothing, rig edits, or added accessories. Camera is the untouched default third-person follow camera.

requirements.sourceQuote:
A lighthearted training-gym aesthetic: the player is a boxer/martial artist in practice gear (tank top, wraps or gloves, shorts) working out in a no-frills gym corner. The target dummy is a classic red-and-black canvas heavy-bag-style humanoid dummy mounted on a weighted base, evoking boxing gyms and arcade punch-meter machines. Tone is upbeat and casual, not violent or gory — this is presented as a training/fitness minigame rather than a combat-to-defeat scenario, reinforced by the dummy's harmless flinch reaction and the absence of health bars or damage numbers. Sound design leans into satisfying 'thwack'/glove-impact punch sounds reminiscent of classic arcade boxing games. The on-screen hit counter is styled like a gym rep-counter or arcade score display (bold numerals, simple font) to reinforce the training-drill framing.
Visual tone is stylized/cartoonish rather than photorealistic or gory, keeping the experience family-friendly.
Player and dummy character models are generic/unbranded (no licensed characters or IP references).
Setting is a single indoor gym-style room; no outdoor or narrative story elements are needed.
No dialogue, voiceover, or narrative text is required beyond the hit counter UI.
Color palette and lighting are simple/bright (gym lighting) rather than dramatic or moody, matching the low-stakes training theme.
requirements.acceptance: The dummy's imported appearance plus default Lighting settings (no custom rigs) together present a bright, casual gym-training look with zero additional decorative props beyond the selected dummy asset.

runtimeReference.textures: Texture and Decal are supported. Face requires {type:"Enum",enum:"NormalId",value:1} for Top, never enum:"Top". Discover requested images through the Marketplace asset pipeline, preferably as part of a complete reusable component. Inspect and verify the selected image before integration. Do not invent IDs or require the user to supply an image that the worker can discover. If retrieval or verification cannot complete, report the specific gap instead of claiming a replacement satisfies the request.

hierarchy.rule: Manifest slash paths describe separate nested Instances. FindFirstChild and WaitForChild take ONE child name, never a slash path. Never create a Folder whose name combines namespace and /children. Script filenames lose .server.luau, .client.luau, .module.luau or .luau at runtime. Example: BuffUtils.module.luau becomes BuffUtils.

runtimeReference.sceneProperties: Name and Parent come from the path: omit both from properties. BasePart uses Color (Color3 value), Size (Vector3), CFrame, Anchored and CanCollide; it has no Color3 or Scale property. Set a walkable ground surface and a collidable spawn. LocalScripts run in StarterGui or StarterPlayerScripts; shared ModuleScripts in ReplicatedStorage are required explicitly.

references.rule: Part0, Part1, PrimaryPart, Attachment0/1 and Adornee use {type:'Ref',path:'exact scene path'}, never strings or nested Instances. Null path clears a reference. All referenced nodes must be declared in this bundle or existing dependencies. References resolve after construction, so forward references work. Humanoid, Animator, AnimationController, Motor6D, Weld, WeldConstraint and Highlight are supported scene classes. Motor6D requires BasePart Part0/Part1 and CFrame C0/C1. Models containing a Humanoid need a connected, unanchored rig to move, not just disconnected decorative parts.

runtimeReference.animation: Resize individual Parts with Size, recolor with Color, and animate via TweenService:Create(part, TweenInfo.new(seconds), {Size=targetSize, Color=targetColor}). Models scale with ScaleTo(number) and move with PivotTo(CFrame). Do not invent Part.Scale. Keep a crop's bottom above its soil while changing height.
runtimeReference.interactions: ProximityPrompt.Triggered connects on the server and supplies player. Validate humanoid health, distance, rate limits, ownership and current state on the server. Do not trust client attributes or RemoteEvent payloads. Per-player state requires indexing by player/UserId, not just a shared object name; clean associated objects and connections when they leave.
runtimeReference.presentation: A ScreenGui belongs in PlayerGui at runtime; LocalScripts may create it there. Put GUI Frames inside a ScreenGui, not directly inside PlayerGui. For a ResetOnSpawn=false HUD, keep its controller in StarterPlayerScripts or inside that persistent ScreenGui. A LocalScript directly under a StarterGui Folder restarts after respawn and can create duplicate, stale HUDs. Rebind health subscriptions on CharacterAdded and disconnect old connections. Send initial state after the client is ready, or use replicated attributes/value objects that the HUD reads initially and observes for changes. A one-time FireClient during PlayerAdded can be missed.
runtimeReference.audio: Audio is Marketplace-only. Discover complete reusable components first, preserving included sound references and provenance; search separately for missing sounds. Audio must pass the asset pipeline's loading, playback and listening checks before acceptance. Built-in, generated, placeholder and procedural audio are not permitted fallbacks. If verified audio is unavailable, report the unmet requirement rather than silently substituting sound. Do not invent IDs or claim unperformed playback tests.
runtimeReference.verification: FindFirstChild absence is a failure when an object is required: assert its presence before checking behavior. Tests must not skip absent objects, compare fabricated state tables, or call nonexistent signal Fire methods. Keep tests out of the live player loop; use the protected review harness for acceptance tests. Report untestable interactions honestly.

spec.title: Punch the Dummy: Training Drill
spec.summary: A minimal single-player boxing-gym practice loop. The player spawns on a plain, undecorated floor a short walk from a stationary training dummy (selected asset 1245720733), using the default Roblox avatar, default third-person camera and default WASD/gamepad movement with no arena boundaries. Pressing the single punch input (left click, Space, or gamepad A) triggers a forward jab (R15 Punching Animations asset 12061946559, clip 1/1/18/1) lasting roughly 0.3-0.5s (windup/strike/recovery) if the player is not already mid-punch. The server authoritatively checks the strike-frame overlap against the dummy's hitbox; on a confirmed hit it plays the Punch Impact 1 sound (asset 132504023010884) once and increments a persistent on-screen 'Hits: N' counter by exactly 1, gated by a per-swing hit-registered flag so only one hit registers per swing even under sustained overlap. The dummy has no health, never flinches, never attacks, and cannot be defeated or moved. There is no reset-counter control; the count persists for the session and only clears on scene reload. No combos, kicks, blocks, scoring, timers or win conditions are included. First minute: player spawns near the dummy on the plain floor, sees the 'Hits: 0' counter top-of-screen, walks up, punches, hears/see the jab animation and impact sound, and watches the counter climb with each successful connect - a simple, satisfying training-drill loop.
spec.visualDirection: Bright, simple default Roblox lighting evokes a no-frills gym corner - no custom lighting rigs, fog, or moody color grading. The only authored visual elements are the imported dummy's own red-and-black canvas heavy-bag styling (asset-provided, not recolored) and a plain flat gray/neutral floor with zero decorative props or backdrop. The HUD is a single bold 'Hits: N' text label anchored to a fixed screen corner (top-center or top-right), styled like a simple arcade rep-counter (bold sans numerals, high-contrast color against a small translucent backing frame) but otherwise unadorned - no meters, health bars, or damage numbers. Player and dummy appearance come entirely from the default Roblox avatar and the selected dummy asset; no custom clothing, rig edits, or added accessories. Camera is the untouched default third-person follow camera.

requirements.description: The full punch loop works end to end: pressing the single punch input while not mid-punch triggers a server-approved punch, plays the animation, checks the strike-frame overlap against the dummy, and on success plays the sound and increments the counter.
requirements.sourceQuote: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.
requirements.acceptance: Pressing the punch input (left click / Space / gamepad A) while not mid-punch produces a full observable cycle: server approval, client animation playback, server hit-window check against the dummy, and on success a synchronized sound plus a +1 counter update, reproducible across repeated swings with correct cooldown gating.

requirements.description: The player cannot chain or spam punches: a punch action can only start if the player is not already mid-punch, and only one hit registers per swing even if dummy overlap persists across multiple frames.
requirements.sourceQuote:
Core loop: the player (default Roblox avatar) faces the selected stationary target dummy asset. Pressing a single 'Punch' input (default: left mouse click or gamepad face button A / keyboard Space) triggers a punch action if the player is not already mid-punch (no combo chaining). The punch action plays a forward jab animation lasting roughly 0.3-0.5 seconds (windup, strike, recovery). A hit is registered when the punch's active strike frame overlaps the dummy's hitbox. On a successful hit: (1) a punch/hit sound effect plays once, (2) the on-screen hit counter increments by exactly 1. A brief cooldown ensures only one hit is registered per punch swing, even if overlap persists across multiple frames. The dummy has no health, cannot be defeated, never attacks back, and shows no flinch or reactive animation. There is no reset-counter control; the counter persists for the play session and resets only on scene reload/restart. Player movement uses standard default Roblox movement controls (WASD/left stick) with no added arena boundaries or movement restrictions beyond the default playable space; no jumping or blocking mechanics are included in this scope.
Single-player only; no multiplayer, AI opponent behavior, or networking.
Dummy is purely stationary and cannot be damaged, destroyed, or knocked over, and has no flinch or reactive animation.

requirements.acceptance: Server rejects a new RequestPunch while the player's per-player mid-punch/cooldown flag is true; a per-swing hit-registered flag ensures at most one hit is counted per swing regardless of how long strike-window overlap with the dummy lasts.

requirements.description: The scene reads as a lighthearted training-gym aesthetic using the selected dummy's existing red/black canvas styling and default bright Roblox lighting, with no added decoration.
requirements.sourceQuote:
A lighthearted training-gym aesthetic: the player is a boxer/martial artist in practice gear (tank top, wraps or gloves, shorts) working out in a no-frills gym corner. The target dummy is a classic red-and-black canvas heavy-bag-style humanoid dummy mounted on a weighted base, evoking boxing gyms and arcade punch-meter machines. Tone is upbeat and casual, not violent or gory — this is presented as a training/fitness minigame rather than a combat-to-defeat scenario, reinforced by the dummy's harmless flinch reaction and the absence of health bars or damage numbers. Sound design leans into satisfying 'thwack'/glove-impact punch sounds reminiscent of classic arcade boxing games. The on-screen hit counter is styled like a gym rep-counter or arcade score display (bold numerals, simple font) to reinforce the training-drill framing.
Visual tone is stylized/cartoonish rather than photorealistic or gory, keeping the experience family-friendly.
Player and dummy character models are generic/unbranded (no licensed characters or IP references).
Setting is a single indoor gym-style room; no outdoor or narrative story elements are needed.
No dialogue, voiceover, or narrative text is required beyond the hit counter UI.
Color palette and lighting are simple/bright (gym lighting) rather than dramatic or moody, matching the low-stakes training theme.
requirements.acceptance: The dummy's imported appearance plus default Lighting settings (no custom rigs) together present a bright, casual gym-training look with zero additional decorative props beyond the selected dummy asset.

playerExperience.title: Punch the Dummy: Training Drill
playerExperience.summary: A minimal single-player boxing-gym practice loop. The player spawns on a plain, undecorated floor a short walk from a stationary training dummy (selected asset 1245720733), using the default Roblox avatar, default third-person camera and default WASD/gamepad movement with no arena boundaries. Pressing the single punch input (left click, Space, or gamepad A) triggers a forward jab (R15 Punching Animations asset 12061946559, clip 1/1/18/1) lasting roughly 0.3-0.5s (windup/strike/recovery) if the player is not already mid-punch. The server authoritatively checks the strike-frame overlap against the dummy's hitbox; on a confirmed hit it plays the Punch Impact 1 sound (asset 132504023010884) once and increments a persistent on-screen 'Hits: N' counter by exactly 1, gated by a per-swing hit-registered flag so only one hit registers per swing even under sustained overlap. The dummy has no health, never flinches, never attacks, and cannot be defeated or moved. There is no reset-counter control; the count persists for the session and only clears on scene reload. No combos, kicks, blocks, scoring, timers or win conditions are included. First minute: player spawns near the dummy on the plain floor, sees the 'Hits: 0' counter top-of-screen, walks up, punches, hears/see the jab animation and impact sound, and watches the counter climb with each successful connect - a simple, satisfying training-drill loop.
playerExperience.visualDirection: Bright, simple default Roblox lighting evokes a no-frills gym corner - no custom lighting rigs, fog, or moody color grading. The only authored visual elements are the imported dummy's own red-and-black canvas heavy-bag styling (asset-provided, not recolored) and a plain flat gray/neutral floor with zero decorative props or backdrop. The HUD is a single bold 'Hits: N' text label anchored to a fixed screen corner (top-center or top-right), styled like a simple arcade rep-counter (bold sans numerals, high-contrast color against a small translucent backing frame) but otherwise unadorned - no meters, health bars, or damage numbers. Player and dummy appearance come entirely from the default Roblox avatar and the selected dummy asset; no custom clothing, rig edits, or added accessories. Camera is the untouched default third-person follow camera.

requirements.description: The scene reads as a lighthearted training-gym aesthetic using the selected dummy's existing red/black canvas styling and default bright Roblox lighting, with no added decoration.
requirements.sourceQuote:
A lighthearted training-gym aesthetic: the player is a boxer/martial artist in practice gear (tank top, wraps or gloves, shorts) working out in a no-frills gym corner. The target dummy is a classic red-and-black canvas heavy-bag-style humanoid dummy mounted on a weighted base, evoking boxing gyms and arcade punch-meter machines. Tone is upbeat and casual, not violent or gory — this is presented as a training/fitness minigame rather than a combat-to-defeat scenario, reinforced by the dummy's harmless flinch reaction and the absence of health bars or damage numbers. Sound design leans into satisfying 'thwack'/glove-impact punch sounds reminiscent of classic arcade boxing games. The on-screen hit counter is styled like a gym rep-counter or arcade score display (bold numerals, simple font) to reinforce the training-drill framing.
Visual tone is stylized/cartoonish rather than photorealistic or gory, keeping the experience family-friendly.
Player and dummy character models are generic/unbranded (no licensed characters or IP references).
Setting is a single indoor gym-style room; no outdoor or narrative story elements are needed.
No dialogue, voiceover, or narrative text is required beyond the hit counter UI.
Color palette and lighting are simple/bright (gym lighting) rather than dramatic or moody, matching the low-stakes training theme.
requirements.acceptance: The dummy's imported appearance plus default Lighting settings (no custom rigs) together present a bright, casual gym-training look with zero additional decorative props beyond the selected dummy asset.

runtimeReference.textures: Texture and Decal are supported. Face requires {type:"Enum",enum:"NormalId",value:1} for Top, never enum:"Top". Discover requested images through the Marketplace asset pipeline, preferably as part of a complete reusable component. Inspect and verify the selected image before integration. Do not invent IDs or require the user to supply an image that the worker can discover. If retrieval or verification cannot complete, report the specific gap instead of claiming a replacement satisfies the request.

hierarchy.rule: Manifest slash paths describe separate nested Instances. FindFirstChild and WaitForChild take ONE child name, never a slash path. Never create a Folder whose name combines namespace and /children. Script filenames lose .server.luau, .client.luau, .module.luau or .luau at runtime. Example: BuffUtils.module.luau becomes BuffUtils.

runtimeReference.sceneProperties: Name and Parent come from the path: omit both from properties. BasePart uses Color (Color3 value), Size (Vector3), CFrame, Anchored and CanCollide; it has no Color3 or Scale property. Set a walkable ground surface and a collidable spawn. LocalScripts run in StarterGui or StarterPlayerScripts; shared ModuleScripts in ReplicatedStorage are required explicitly.

references.rule: Part0, Part1, PrimaryPart, Attachment0/1 and Adornee use {type:'Ref',path:'exact scene path'}, never strings or nested Instances. Null path clears a reference. All referenced nodes must be declared in this bundle or existing dependencies. References resolve after construction, so forward references work. Humanoid, Animator, AnimationController, Motor6D, Weld, WeldConstraint and Highlight are supported scene classes. Motor6D requires BasePart Part0/Part1 and CFrame C0/C1. Models containing a Humanoid need a connected, unanchored rig to move, not just disconnected decorative parts.

runtimeReference.animation: Resize individual Parts with Size, recolor with Color, and animate via TweenService:Create(part, TweenInfo.new(seconds), {Size=targetSize, Color=targetColor}). Models scale with ScaleTo(number) and move with PivotTo(CFrame). Do not invent Part.Scale. Keep a crop's bottom above its soil while changing height.
runtimeReference.interactions: ProximityPrompt.Triggered connects on the server and supplies player. Validate humanoid health, distance, rate limits, ownership and current state on the server. Do not trust client attributes or RemoteEvent payloads. Per-player state requires indexing by player/UserId, not just a shared object name; clean associated objects and connections when they leave.
runtimeReference.presentation: A ScreenGui belongs in PlayerGui at runtime; LocalScripts may create it there. Put GUI Frames inside a ScreenGui, not directly inside PlayerGui. For a ResetOnSpawn=false HUD, keep its controller in StarterPlayerScripts or inside that persistent ScreenGui. A LocalScript directly under a StarterGui Folder restarts after respawn and can create duplicate, stale HUDs. Rebind health subscriptions on CharacterAdded and disconnect old connections. Send initial state after the client is ready, or use replicated attributes/value objects that the HUD reads initially and observes for changes. A one-time FireClient during PlayerAdded can be missed.
runtimeReference.audio: Audio is Marketplace-only. Discover complete reusable components first, preserving included sound references and provenance; search separately for missing sounds. Audio must pass the asset pipeline's loading, playback and listening checks before acceptance. Built-in, generated, placeholder and procedural audio are not permitted fallbacks. If verified audio is unavailable, report the unmet requirement rather than silently substituting sound. Do not invent IDs or claim unperformed playback tests.
runtimeReference.verification: FindFirstChild absence is a failure when an object is required: assert its presence before checking behavior. Tests must not skip absent objects, compare fabricated state tables, or call nonexistent signal Fire methods. Keep tests out of the live player loop; use the protected review harness for acceptance tests. Report untestable interactions honestly.

spec.title: Punch the Dummy: Training Drill
spec.summary: A minimal single-player boxing-gym practice loop. The player spawns on a plain, undecorated floor a short walk from a stationary training dummy (selected asset 1245720733), using the default Roblox avatar, default third-person camera and default WASD/gamepad movement with no arena boundaries. Pressing the single punch input (left click, Space, or gamepad A) triggers a forward jab (R15 Punching Animations asset 12061946559, clip 1/1/18/1) lasting roughly 0.3-0.5s (windup/strike/recovery) if the player is not already mid-punch. The server authoritatively checks the strike-frame overlap against the dummy's hitbox; on a confirmed hit it plays the Punch Impact 1 sound (asset 132504023010884) once and increments a persistent on-screen 'Hits: N' counter by exactly 1, gated by a per-swing hit-registered flag so only one hit registers per swing even under sustained overlap. The dummy has no health, never flinches, never attacks, and cannot be defeated or moved. There is no reset-counter control; the count persists for the session and only clears on scene reload. No combos, kicks, blocks, scoring, timers or win conditions are included. First minute: player spawns near the dummy on the plain floor, sees the 'Hits: 0' counter top-of-screen, walks up, punches, hears/see the jab animation and impact sound, and watches the counter climb with each successful connect - a simple, satisfying training-drill loop.
spec.visualDirection: Bright, simple default Roblox lighting evokes a no-frills gym corner - no custom lighting rigs, fog, or moody color grading. The only authored visual elements are the imported dummy's own red-and-black canvas heavy-bag styling (asset-provided, not recolored) and a plain flat gray/neutral floor with zero decorative props or backdrop. The HUD is a single bold 'Hits: N' text label anchored to a fixed screen corner (top-center or top-right), styled like a simple arcade rep-counter (bold sans numerals, high-contrast color against a small translucent backing frame) but otherwise unadorned - no meters, health bars, or damage numbers. Player and dummy appearance come entirely from the default Roblox avatar and the selected dummy asset; no custom clothing, rig edits, or added accessories. Camera is the untouched default third-person follow camera.

requirements.description: The full punch loop works end to end: pressing the single punch input while not mid-punch triggers a server-approved punch, plays the animation, checks the strike-frame overlap against the dummy, and on success plays the sound and increments the counter.
requirements.sourceQuote: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.
requirements.acceptance: Pressing the punch input (left click / Space / gamepad A) while not mid-punch produces a full observable cycle: server approval, client animation playback, server hit-window check against the dummy, and on success a synchronized sound plus a +1 counter update, reproducible across repeated swings with correct cooldown gating.

requirements.description: The player cannot chain or spam punches: a punch action can only start if the player is not already mid-punch, and only one hit registers per swing even if dummy overlap persists across multiple frames.

playerExperience.summary: A minimal single-player boxing-gym practice loop. The player spawns on a plain, undecorated floor a short walk from a stationary training dummy (selected asset 1245720733), using the default Roblox avatar, default third-person camera and default WASD/gamepad movement with no arena boundaries. Pressing the single punch input (left click, Space, or gamepad A) triggers a forward jab (R15 Punching Animations asset 12061946559, clip 1/1/18/1) lasting roughly 0.3-0.5s (windup/strike/recovery) if the player is not already mid-punch. The server authoritatively checks the strike-frame overlap against the dummy's hitbox; on a confirmed hit it plays the Punch Impact 1 sound (asset 132504023010884) once and increments a persistent on-screen 'Hits: N' counter by exactly 1, gated by a per-swing hit-registered flag so only one hit registers per swing even under sustained overlap. The dummy has no health, never flinches, never attacks, and cannot be defeated or moved. There is no reset-counter control; the count persists for the session and only clears on scene reload. No combos, kicks, blocks, scoring, timers or win conditions are included. First minute: player spawns near the dummy on the plain floor, sees the 'Hits: 0' counter top-of-screen, walks up, punches, hears/see the jab animation and impact sound, and watches the counter climb with each successful connect - a simple, satisfying training-drill loop.

The HUD is a single bold 'Hits: N' text label anchored to a fixed screen corner (top-center or top-right), styled like a simple arcade rep-counter (bold sans numerals, high-contrast color against a small translucent backing frame) but otherwise unadorned - no meters, health bars, or damage numbers. requirements.description: The scene reads as a lighthearted training-gym aesthetic using the selected dummy's existing red/black canvas styling and default bright Roblox lighting, with no added decoration.
requirements.sourceQuote:
A lighthearted training-gym aesthetic: the player is a boxer/martial artist in practice gear (tank top, wraps or gloves, shorts) working out in a no-frills gym corner. The target dummy is a classic red-and-black canvas heavy-bag-style humanoid dummy mounted on a weighted base, evoking boxing gyms and arcade punch-meter machines. Tone is upbeat and casual, not violent or gory — this is presented as a training/fitness minigame rather than a combat-to-defeat scenario, reinforced by the dummy's harmless flinch reaction and the absence of health bars or damage numbers. Sound design leans into satisfying 'thwack'/glove-impact punch sounds reminiscent of classic arcade boxing games. The on-screen hit counter is styled like a gym rep-counter or arcade score display (bold numerals, simple font) to reinforce the training-drill framing.
Visual tone is stylized/cartoonish rather than photorealistic or gory, keeping the experience family-friendly.
Player and dummy character models are generic/unbranded (no licensed characters or IP references).
Setting is a single indoor gym-style room; no outdoor or narrative story elements are needed.
No dialogue, voiceover, or narrative text is required beyond the hit counter UI.
Color palette and lighting are simple/bright (gym lighting) rather than dramatic or moody, matching the low-stakes training theme.
requirements.acceptance: The dummy's imported appearance plus default Lighting settings (no custom rigs) together present a bright, casual gym-training look with zero additional decorative props beyond the selected dummy asset.

runtimeReference.textures: Texture and Decal are supported. Face requires {type:"Enum",enum:"NormalId",value:1} for Top, never enum:"Top". Discover requested images through the Marketplace asset pipeline, preferably as part of a complete reusable component. Inspect and verify the selected image before integration. Do not invent IDs or require the user to supply an image that the worker can discover. If retrieval or verification cannot complete, report the specific gap instead of claiming a replacement satisfies the request.

hierarchy.rule: Manifest slash paths describe separate nested Instances. FindFirstChild and WaitForChild take ONE child name, never a slash path. Never create a Folder whose name combines namespace and /children. Script filenames lose .server.luau, .client.luau, .module.luau or .luau at runtime. Example: BuffUtils.module.luau becomes BuffUtils.

runtimeReference.sceneProperties: Name and Parent come from the path: omit both from properties. BasePart uses Color (Color3 value), Size (Vector3), CFrame, Anchored and CanCollide; it has no Color3 or Scale property. Set a walkable ground surface and a collidable spawn. LocalScripts run in StarterGui or StarterPlayerScripts; shared ModuleScripts in ReplicatedStorage are required explicitly.

references.rule: Part0, Part1, PrimaryPart, Attachment0/1 and Adornee use {type:'Ref',path:'exact scene path'}, never strings or nested Instances. Null path clears a reference. All referenced nodes must be declared in this bundle or existing dependencies. References resolve after construction, so forward references work. Humanoid, Animator, AnimationController, Motor6D, Weld, WeldConstraint and Highlight are supported scene classes. Motor6D requires BasePart Part0/Part1 and CFrame C0/C1. Models containing a Humanoid need a connected, unanchored rig to move, not just disconnected decorative parts.

runtimeReference.animation: Resize individual Parts with Size, recolor with Color, and animate via TweenService:Create(part, TweenInfo.new(seconds), {Size=targetSize, Color=targetColor}). Models scale with ScaleTo(number) and move with PivotTo(CFrame). Do not invent Part.Scale. Keep a crop's bottom above its soil while changing height.
runtimeReference.interactions: ProximityPrompt.Triggered connects on the server and supplies player. Validate humanoid health, distance, rate limits, ownership and current state on the server. Do not trust client attributes or RemoteEvent payloads. Per-player state requires indexing by player/UserId, not just a shared object name; clean associated objects and connections when they leave.
runtimeReference.presentation: A ScreenGui belongs in PlayerGui at runtime; LocalScripts may create it there. Put GUI Frames inside a ScreenGui, not directly inside PlayerGui. For a ResetOnSpawn=false HUD, keep its controller in StarterPlayerScripts or inside that persistent ScreenGui. A LocalScript directly under a StarterGui Folder restarts after respawn and can create duplicate, stale HUDs. Rebind health subscriptions on CharacterAdded and disconnect old connections. Send initial state after the client is ready, or use replicated attributes/value objects that the HUD reads initially and observes for changes. A one-time FireClient during PlayerAdded can be missed.
runtimeReference.audio: Audio is Marketplace-only. Discover complete reusable components first, preserving included sound references and provenance; search separately for missing sounds. Audio must pass the asset pipeline's loading, playback and listening checks before acceptance. Built-in, generated, placeholder and procedural audio are not permitted fallbacks. If verified audio is unavailable, report the unmet requirement rather than silently substituting sound. Do not invent IDs or claim unperformed playback tests.
runtimeReference.verification: FindFirstChild absence is a failure when an object is required: assert its presence before checking behavior. Tests must not skip absent objects, compare fabricated state tables, or call nonexistent signal Fire methods. Keep tests out of the live player loop; use the protected review harness for acceptance tests. Report untestable interactions honestly.

nodes.name: PunchAnimationAsset

nodes.name: PunchImpactSoundAsset

nodes.name: PunchInputController
nodes.purpose: Captures the single punch input (click/Space/gamepad A), gates re-trigger while mid-punch, and requests a punch from the server; plays the approved animation and rebinds on respawn.

nodes.name: PunchServer
nodes.purpose: Authoritative punch handler: validates cooldown/mid-punch state and player health, checks strike-window overlap against the dummy hitbox, and coordinates approved-animation playback, hit confirmation, sound trigger and counter increment.

nodes.name: HitDetectionModule
nodes.purpose: Shared per-player cooldown/mid-punch state tracking plus the distance/hitbox overlap math used to decide exactly one hit per swing.

nodes.name: HitCounterService
nodes.purpose: Tracks each player's session hit count keyed by UserId and replicates updates to that player's HUD; cleans up on PlayerRemoving.

nodes.name: HitCounterHud
nodes.purpose: Displays the persistent 'Hits: N' on-screen counter anchored to a fixed screen corner; has no reset control and survives respawns.

spec.assetStrategy: Three Marketplace assets were already selected by the user and must be preserved and integrated rather than replaced: (1) 'Training Dummy' (1245720733) supplies the stationary target's full appearance and geometry - its single embedded script must be inspected before deciding whether to keep or disable it, since the requirement is a purely stationary, non-reactive dummy; (2) 'R15 Punching Animations' (12061946559) supplies the forward jab clip at embedded key 1/1/18/1, which must be located, verified as R15-compatible with the default avatar, and exposed for Animator playback - per the standalone-animation limitation, this is sourced as a Model pack rather than a bare Animation asset; (3) 'Punch Impact 1' (132504023010884) supplies the one-shot hit sound, which must be verified for load/playback/listening before being wired to the server's hit-confirmation path. No additional decorative, environment, or animation Marketplace searches are needed given the deliberately minimal scope (plain floor, default avatar, default camera). Missing integration work is limited to: parenting/positioning the dummy and its hitbox reference, extracting and playing the specific punch clip on server-approved requests, and triggering/parenting the impact sound near the dummy for server-controlled playback. All hit validation, cooldown, and counter logic are original small server-authoritative scripts/modules, since no Marketplace behavior was selected or requested for those systems.
spec.title: Punch the Dummy: Training Drill
spec.summary: A minimal single-player boxing-gym practice loop. The player spawns on a plain, undecorated floor a short walk from a stationary training dummy (selected asset 1245720733), using the default Roblox avatar, default third-person camera and default WASD/gamepad movement with no arena boundaries. Pressing the single punch input (left click, Space, or gamepad A) triggers a forward jab (R15 Punching Animations asset 12061946559, clip 1/1/18/1) lasting roughly 0.3-0.5s (windup/strike/recovery) if the player is not already mid-punch. The server authoritatively checks the strike-frame overlap against the dummy's hitbox; on a confirmed hit it plays the Punch Impact 1 sound (asset 132504023010884) once and increments a persistent on-screen 'Hits: N' counter by exactly 1, gated by a per-swing hit-registered flag so only one hit registers per swing even under sustained overlap. The dummy has no health, never flinches, never attacks, and cannot be defeated or moved. There is no reset-counter control; the count persists for the session and only clears on scene reload. No combos, kicks, blocks, scoring, timers or win conditions are included. First minute: player spawns near the dummy on the plain floor, sees the 'Hits: 0' counter top-of-screen, walks up, punches, hears/see the jab animation and impact sound, and watches the counter climb with each successful connect - a simple, satisfying training-drill loop.
spec.visualDirection: Bright, simple default Roblox lighting evokes a no-frills gym corner - no custom lighting rigs, fog, or moody color grading. The only authored visual elements are the imported dummy's own red-and-black canvas heavy-bag styling (asset-provided, not recolored) and a plain flat gray/neutral floor with zero decorative props or backdrop. The HUD is a single bold 'Hits: N' text label anchored to a fixed screen corner (top-center or top-right), styled like a simple arcade rep-counter (bold sans numerals, high-contrast color against a small translucent backing frame) but otherwise unadorned - no meters, health bars, or damage numbers. Player and dummy appearance come entirely from the default Roblox avatar and the selected dummy asset; no custom clothing, rig edits, or added accessories. Camera is the untouched default third-person follow camera.

requirements.description: The full punch loop works end to end: pressing the single punch input while not mid-punch triggers a server-approved punch, plays the animation, checks the strike-frame overlap against the dummy, and on success plays the sound and increments the counter.
requirements.sourceQuote: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.
requirements.acceptance: Pressing the punch input (left click / Space / gamepad A) while not mid-punch produces a full observable cycle: server approval, client animation playback, server hit-window check against the dummy, and on success a synchronized sound plus a +1 counter update, reproducible across repeated swings with correct cooldown gating.

requirements.description: The player cannot chain or spam punches: a punch action can only start if the player is not already mid-punch, and only one hit registers per swing even if dummy overlap persists across multiple frames.
requirements.sourceQuote:
Core loop: the player (default Roblox avatar) faces the selected stationary target dummy asset. Pressing a single 'Punch' input (default: left mouse click or gamepad face button A / keyboard Space) triggers a punch action if the player is not already mid-punch (no combo chaining). The punch action plays a forward jab animation lasting roughly 0.3-0.5 seconds (windup, strike, recovery). A hit is registered when the punch's active strike frame overlaps the dummy's hitbox. On a successful hit: (1) a punch/hit sound effect plays once, (2) the on-screen hit counter increments by exactly 1. A brief cooldown ensures only one hit is registered per punch swing, even if overlap persists across multiple frames. The dummy has no health, cannot be defeated, never attacks back, and shows no flinch or reactive animation. There is no reset-counter control; the counter persists for the play session and resets only on scene reload/restart. Player movement uses standard default Roblox movement controls (WASD/left stick) with no added arena boundaries or movement restrictions beyond the default playable space; no jumping or blocking mechanics are included in this scope.
Single-player only; no multiplayer, AI opponent behavior, or networking.
Dummy is purely stationary and cannot be damaged, destroyed, or knocked over, and has no flinch or reactive animation.
Only one punch type/animation is required (no combos, kicks, blocks, or special moves) per the request scope.
Hit counter is a simple integer displayed as on-screen UI text (e.g., 'Hits: 0') anchored to a screen corner.
Counter increments exactly once per successful punch connection using a per-swing hit-registered flag.
Default control scheme: standard Roblox movement plus one button for punching; no reset-counter input or button is included.
No scoring, timer, win condition, or difficulty progression is required; this is a practice/demo loop.
Punch and hit use the same single sound effect (no separate whiff vs. connect sounds) unless later expanded.
Player avatar and dummy appearance are provided entirely by the selected default/selected Roblox assets; no custom clothing or rig modifications are required.
Camera uses the default Roblox third-person follow camera; no fixed framing or custom camera control is implemented.
requirements.acceptance: Server rejects a new RequestPunch while the player's per-player mid-punch/cooldown flag is true; a per-swing hit-registered flag ensures at most one hit is counted per swing regardless of how long strike-window overlap with the dummy lasts.

requirements.description: The scene reads as a lighthearted training-gym aesthetic using the selected dummy's existing red/black canvas styling and default bright Roblox lighting, with no added decoration.
requirements.sourceQuote:
A lighthearted training-gym aesthetic: the player is a boxer/martial artist in practice gear (tank top, wraps or gloves, shorts) working out in a no-frills gym corner. The target dummy is a classic red-and-black canvas heavy-bag-style humanoid dummy mounted on a weighted base, evoking boxing gyms and arcade punch-meter machines. Tone is upbeat and casual, not violent or gory — this is presented as a training/fitness minigame rather than a combat-to-defeat scenario, reinforced by the dummy's harmless flinch reaction and the absence of health bars or damage numbers. Sound design leans into satisfying 'thwack'/glove-impact punch sounds reminiscent of classic arcade boxing games. The on-screen hit counter is styled like a gym rep-counter or arcade score display (bold numerals, simple font) to reinforce the training-drill framing.
Visual tone is stylized/cartoonish rather than photorealistic or gory, keeping the experience family-friendly.
Player and dummy character models are generic/unbranded (no licensed characters or IP references).
Setting is a single indoor gym-style room; no outdoor or narrative story elements are needed.
No dialogue, voiceover, or narrative text is required beyond the hit counter UI.
Color palette and lighting are simple/bright (gym lighting) rather than dramatic or moody, matching the low-stakes training theme.
requirements.acceptance: The dummy's imported appearance plus default Lighting settings (no custom rigs) together present a bright, casual gym-training look with zero additional decorative props beyond the selected dummy asset.

approvedProposal.title: Punch the Dummy: Training Drill

mechanics.text: Core loop: the player (default Roblox avatar) faces the selected stationary target dummy asset. Pressing a single 'Punch' input (default: left mouse click or gamepad face button A / keyboard Space) triggers a punch action if the player is not already mid-punch (no combo chaining). The punch action plays a forward jab animation lasting roughly 0.3-0.5 seconds (windup, strike, recovery). A hit is registered when the punch's active strike frame overlaps the dummy's hitbox. On a successful hit: (1) a punch/hit sound effect plays once, (2) the on-screen hit counter increments by exactly 1. A brief cooldown ensures only one hit is registered per punch swing, even if overlap persists across multiple frames. The dummy has no health, cannot be defeated, never attacks back, and shows no flinch or reactive animation. There is no reset-counter control; the counter persists for the play session and resets only on scene reload/restart. Player movement uses standard default Roblox movement controls (WASD/left stick) with no added arena boundaries or movement restrictions beyond the default playable space; no jumping or blocking mechanics are included in this scope.
assumptions: Single-player only; no multiplayer, AI opponent behavior, or networking.
Dummy is purely stationary and cannot be damaged, destroyed, or knocked over, and has no flinch or reactive animation.
Only one punch type/animation is required (no combos, kicks, blocks, or special moves) per the request scope.
Hit counter is a simple integer displayed as on-screen UI text (e.g., 'Hits: 0') anchored to a screen corner.
Counter increments exactly once per successful punch connection using a per-swing hit-registered flag.
Default control scheme: standard Roblox movement plus one button for punching; no reset-counter input or button is included.
No scoring, timer, win condition, or difficulty progression is required; this is a practice/demo loop.
Punch and hit use the same single sound effect (no separate whiff vs. connect sounds) unless later expanded.
Player avatar and dummy appearance are provided entirely by the selected default/selected Roblox assets; no custom clothing or rig modifications are required.
Camera uses the default Roblox third-person follow camera; no fixed framing or custom camera control is implemented.

theme.text: A lighthearted training-gym aesthetic: the player is a boxer/martial artist in practice gear (tank top, wraps or gloves, shorts) working out in a no-frills gym corner. The target dummy is a classic red-and-black canvas heavy-bag-style humanoid dummy mounted on a weighted base, evoking boxing gyms and arcade punch-meter machines. Tone is upbeat and casual, not violent or gory — this is presented as a training/fitness minigame rather than a combat-to-defeat scenario, reinforced by the dummy's harmless flinch reaction and the absence of health bars or damage numbers. Sound design leans into satisfying 'thwack'/glove-impact punch sounds reminiscent of classic arcade boxing games. The on-screen hit counter is styled like a gym rep-counter or arcade score display (bold numerals, simple font) to reinforce the training-drill framing.
assumptions: Visual tone is stylized/cartoonish rather than photorealistic or gory, keeping the experience family-friendly.
Player and dummy character models are generic/unbranded (no licensed characters or IP references).
Setting is a single indoor gym-style room; no outdoor or narrative story elements are needed.
No dialogue, voiceover, or narrative text is required beyond the hit counter UI.
Color palette and lighting are simple/bright (gym lighting) rather than dramatic or moody, matching the low-stakes training theme.

environment.text: Layout is a plain flat floor with no additional decoration, props, or themed backdrop. The selected stationary target dummy asset is placed at a fixed point on the floor; the player spawns using the default Roblox avatar a short distance away, within comfortable punching range after a short walk. The on-screen hit counter UI is anchored to a fixed screen-space position (e.g., top-center or top-right) so it remains visible during gameplay. The scene uses the default Roblox camera (third-person follow) with no custom framing. There are no invisible walls, arena boundaries, or added movement restrictions; the player can move freely across the plain floor using standard default movement, relying on default Roblox physics and collision.
assumptions: Single static scene; no level transitions, multiple rooms, or loading between areas.
Play space is a plain floor with no decorative props, backdrop, or themed environment art; only the selected dummy asset and default avatar are present.
Lighting uses Roblox default lighting; no custom or dynamic lighting rigs are configured.
No destructible or interactive environment props beyond the dummy itself in this scope.
No arena boundaries or invisible walls are added; player movement is unrestricted beyond the standard default playable area.

playerExperience.title: Punch the Dummy: Training Drill
playerExperience.summary: A minimal single-player boxing-gym practice loop. The player spawns on a plain, undecorated floor a short walk from a stationary training dummy (selected asset 1245720733), using the default Roblox avatar, default third-person camera and default WASD/gamepad movement with no arena boundaries. Pressing the single punch input (left click, Space, or gamepad A) triggers a forward jab (R15 Punching Animations asset 12061946559, clip 1/1/18/1) lasting roughly 0.3-0.5s (windup/strike/recovery) if the player is not already mid-punch. The server authoritatively checks the strike-frame overlap against the dummy's hitbox; on a confirmed hit it plays the Punch Impact 1 sound (asset 132504023010884) once and increments a persistent on-screen 'Hits: N' counter by exactly 1, gated by a per-swing hit-registered flag so only one hit registers per swing even under sustained overlap. The dummy has no health, never flinches, never attacks, and cannot be defeated or moved. There is no reset-counter control; the count persists for the session and only clears on scene reload. No combos, kicks, blocks, scoring, timers or win conditions are included. First minute: player spawns near the dummy on the plain floor, sees the 'Hits: 0' counter top-of-screen, walks up, punches, hears/see the jab animation and impact sound, and watches the counter climb with each successful connect - a simple, satisfying training-drill loop.
playerExperience.visualDirection: Bright, simple default Roblox lighting evokes a no-frills gym corner - no custom lighting rigs, fog, or moody color grading. requirements.description: The player cannot chain or spam punches: a punch action can only start if the player is not already mid-punch, and only one hit registers per swing even if dummy overlap persists across multiple frames.

Pressing a single 'Punch' input (default: left mouse click or gamepad face button A / keyboard Space) triggers a punch action if the player is not already mid-punch (no combo chaining). requirements.description: The scene reads as a lighthearted training-gym aesthetic using the selected dummy's existing red/black canvas styling and default bright Roblox lighting, with no added decoration.
requirements.sourceQuote:
A lighthearted training-gym aesthetic: the player is a boxer/martial artist in practice gear (tank top, wraps or gloves, shorts) working out in a no-frills gym corner. The target dummy is a classic red-and-black canvas heavy-bag-style humanoid dummy mounted on a weighted base, evoking boxing gyms and arcade punch-meter machines. Tone is upbeat and casual, not violent or gory — this is presented as a training/fitness minigame rather than a combat-to-defeat scenario, reinforced by the dummy's harmless flinch reaction and the absence of health bars or damage numbers. Sound design leans into satisfying 'thwack'/glove-impact punch sounds reminiscent of classic arcade boxing games. The on-screen hit counter is styled like a gym rep-counter or arcade score display (bold numerals, simple font) to reinforce the training-drill framing.
Visual tone is stylized/cartoonish rather than photorealistic or gory, keeping the experience family-friendly.
Player and dummy character models are generic/unbranded (no licensed characters or IP references).
Setting is a single indoor gym-style room; no outdoor or narrative story elements are needed.
No dialogue, voiceover, or narrative text is required beyond the hit counter UI.
Color palette and lighting are simple/bright (gym lighting) rather than dramatic or moody, matching the low-stakes training theme.
requirements.acceptance: The dummy's imported appearance plus default Lighting settings (no custom rigs) together present a bright, casual gym-training look with zero additional decorative props beyond the selected dummy asset.

playerExperience.assetStrategy: Three Marketplace assets were already selected by the user and must be preserved and integrated rather than replaced: (1) 'Training Dummy' (1245720733) supplies the stationary target's full appearance and geometry - its single embedded script must be inspected before deciding whether to keep or disable it, since the requirement is a purely stationary, non-reactive dummy; (2) 'R15 Punching Animations' (12061946559) supplies the forward jab clip at embedded key 1/1/18/1, which must be located, verified as R15-compatible with the default avatar, and exposed for Animator playback - per the standalone-animation limitation, this is sourced as a Model pack rather than a bare Animation asset; (3) 'Punch Impact 1' (132504023010884) supplies the one-shot hit sound, which must be verified for load/playback/listening before being wired to the server's hit-confirmation path. No additional decorative, environment, or animation Marketplace searches are needed given the deliberately minimal scope (plain floor, default avatar, default camera). Missing integration work is limited to: parenting/positioning the dummy and its hitbox reference, extracting and playing the specific punch clip on server-approved requests, and triggering/parenting the impact sound near the dummy for server-controlled playback. All hit validation, cooldown, and counter logic are original small server-authoritative scripts/modules, since no Marketplace behavior was selected or requested for those systems.
